title: Plan Q: AI Music & Sound Production
summary: Requirement → style reference → AI generation → select & remix → mix & SFX → licensing check
scenario: Best for short-video BGM, game SFX, podcast intros and ad music — from requirement to usable, licensed audio.

steps.title: Define the requirement
steps.detail: Pin the use (BGM / song / SFX / podcast intro), duration, mood and style (genre, tempo, instrumental vs vocal, with or without lyrics).
steps.tips: Write 'mood + scene + style' as a one-line requirement instead of abstract adjectives.

steps.title: Style reference
steps.detail: Describe reference tracks or style keywords and have the AI build an executable prompt (instruments, BPM, harmony, texture); give reference songs to extract features from.
steps.tips: A three-part prompt — reference style + concrete instruments + emotional arc — lands much closer to the brief.

steps.title: AI generation
steps.detail: Suno for complete songs with vocals in any style, Udio for a more 'finished' feel with remixing; generate several versions and pick. Write lyrics with AI, then human-review.
steps.tips: Generate 5-10 takes of the same prompt and refine the best — faster than micro-tuning parameters.

steps.title: Select and remix
steps.detail: Remix / extend / tempo-shift the chosen take; AIVA for classical and pure-instrumental scoring; adapt the 'half-finished' track to your exact length.
steps.tips: Generate the longest usable version and cut down; keep the main melody intact when remixing.

steps.title: Mix and SFX
steps.detail: Layer sound effects (Stable Audio), balance levels and loudness, and stem-separate vocals (Demucs) when you need an instrumental or a remix.
steps.tips: Normalize to the target platform's loudness; in background-music contexts always keep it under the voice floor.

steps.title: Licensing check
steps.detail: Confirm commercial rights for the generated track (Suno paid tier allows commercial use, free tier is limited), attribution rules and platform revenue share.
steps.tips: Read the terms line by line before commercial use — 'can I use a free-tier track commercially' is the most common landmine.

pitfalls.title: Unclear commercial rights
pitfalls.detail: Free-tier tracks carry commercial risk; for commercial use, pay the tier and confirm the license.

pitfalls.title: Robotic AI vocals
pitfalls.detail: Long AI-vocal phrases sound stiff; split sentences, add emotion tags, or audition more takes.

pitfalls.title: Style misses the brief
pitfalls.detail: Abstract prompts drift; use the structured 'reference style + instruments + BPM + mood' form.

pitfalls.title: Poor stem separation
pitfalls.detail: Crude separation sounds scratchy; use a dedicated model like Demucs, or keep the original.
